issues.description: Class Animal: the problem statement and UML require the name accessor methods (getter and setter) to use protected visibility to restrict external access while allowing subclass inheritance. The solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) defines getName() and setName(...) as public methods. This mismatch between the specification (protected) and the solution (public) creates ambiguity for students about the intended encapsulation and access level for subclasses and external code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent with the problem statement and UML. Change the accessor declarations in the solution/template to protected (protected String getName() and protected void setName(String)), or alternatively update the problem statement/UML to require public accessors. Prefer updating the solution/template to use protected accessors so the code matches the stated exercise requirement and demonstrates the intended encapsulation for subclasses.
